A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 16-page versions of CoreGuard, with matching main sections and Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-stealing, accuracy, and overhead experiments in Section 4, plus authorization-position and adaptive-attack results in Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–6 and Figures 2–3. Their retention qualifies even though the results are unchanged.

M1.justification: The written method is unchanged. However, Figure 1 moves permutations from after the TEE's Add & Norm operation in v2 to its two inputs in v3, while Equation (12) still permutes afterward. The PDFs do not clarify whether this represents equivalent rewiring with suitably permuted normalization parameters or an intended procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8k, Spider, PubMedQA, and SQuAD. Direct inference, model stealing, task-alignment scenarios, and adaptive-attack coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains No-shield, NPLO, Serdab, DarkneTZ, SOTER, TLG, ShadowNet, DTE, and Black-box. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the overhead and appendix attack comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same model configurations, accuracy and FLOPs metrics, attacker-data settings, and testing procedures. The overhead evaluation still uses a length-128 input and measures generation of one token.

E4.justification: Figure 2 retains the FFT/LoRA, task-alignment, and training-data analyses. Appendix B's authorization-position study and Appendix D's permutation-matrix and authorization-simulation attacks are unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 2, 5, and 6 retain identical ± reporting, and Section 4.1 retains its highest-performing-run reporting statement. No run-count, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 and Figures 2–3 retain their numerical entries and plotted findings. For example, Table 2 reports the same 1.17× relative mean attack accuracy for CoreGuard. No results are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equation (6) replaces expanded permutation expressions with the primed parameters already defined in Equations (2) and (5); these substitutions are mathematically equivalent. The remaining formal reasoning, including Appendix C's security argument, is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about protecting foundational capabilities, propagating a single initial authorization, achieving strong security with low overhead, and preserving accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations of attack resistance, authorization-position effects, and accuracy fluctuations remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same discussion of side channels, GPU TEEs, device-specific implementation limitations, and architecture compatibility.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including Hugging Face, AdamW, the linear learning-rate scheduler, NVIDIA A800 GPUs with 80GB VRAM, and authorization-position guidance. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The same 52 references and research positioning are retained, including comparisons with TEE-based protection and parameter-shuffling approaches.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to Figure 1 terminology, equivalent primed-parameter notation in Equation (6), and the arXiv version/date header. Paragraphs, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands the depicted attention/FFN matrix operations and redraws the authorization path and user/outcome legend. Its panel letters are removed although the caption retains them. Equation (6) has small layout adjustments; all other figures and tables are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: The consistent notation in Equation (6) and more explicit matrix operations in Figure 1 offer limited clarity benefits. However, the diagram's changed permutation placement is not reconciled with the unchanged authorization equation, leaving its intended equivalence uncertain. With the empirical evidence and appendices unchanged, the net effect of these presentation gains and the new procedural ambiguity cannot be judged reliably.
